record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Does there exist an O*-group with exactly two orderings, namely an ordering ≤ and its reverse, where an O*-group is a group in which every partial order extends to a total order making the group totally ordered?

evidence.quote: 3.30. (V. V. Bludov [13]) Does there exist an O ∗ -group with only two orderings: an ordering ≤ and its reverse?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Call a group $G$ an O*-group if every partial order on $G$ that is invariant under both left and right multiplication can be extended to a total order on $G$ that is invariant under both left and right multiplication (i.e. every partial right- and left-invariant order extends to a bi-invariant total order making $G$ a totally ordered group). Given a bi-invariant total order $\le$ on $G$, its reverse $\le^{op}$ (defined by $x \le^{op} y \iff y \le x$) is also a bi-invariant total order. Question: does there exist an O*-group $G$ which admits exactly two bi-invariant total orders, namely some order $\le$ and its reverse $\le^{op}$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up evidence resolving this specific question about the existence of an O*-group whose only bi-invariant total orders are an order and its reverse. The problem is listed as an open question attributed to V. V. Bludov in problem collections on ordered and orderable groups, and no resolution was found.
